_comment: User-editable budget knobs. Dungeon economics (energyCost, maxRoom, maxRunsPerDay) come from config/discovered.json (generated, gitignored) — this file only holds the numbers a human chooses. Session-08: conservative first-session budget, 3 runs at 20 energy each per session-08 brief §5. Session-09: raised to 120/5 per session-09 brief's explicit stated budget ('120 energy this session... covers five runs with margin') for Task 6's five-run stage — the guard-persistence fix landed this session made maxRunsPerSession a REAL cap across process invocations for the first time, and it was still holding at the session-08 conservative value, capping the session at 3 runs before the five-run gate could be attempted. Session-11: raised to 240/12, matching the user's own confirmed REAL daily budget (session-11 brief §6: '240 energy/day dungeon budget, 12 runs at 20 energy') rather than a session-scoped guess — the guard is date-keyed, so this is now a standing calibration to reality, not a one-day bump. Confirmed directly by the user this session (not raised unilaterally) after today's 78/5 spend from sessions 09-10 blocked the session-11 brief's ask of 3 more 20-energy runs. See DECISIONS.md.

forbiddenWoods._potionsComment: PERMANENT as of CLAUDE.md rule 11 (2026-08-20, session 54). Every dungeon run is now a 60-energy juiced Tier-3 entry with 3 Big Heal Juices, one run at a time, so potions are economically sound on every run that happens and the old add-before / remove-after convention (sessions 24, 42, 43, 52) has nothing left to protect against. WHY THAT CONVENTION EXISTED: session 24, a plain 20-energy orchestrator run auto-loaded potions from this block because no juiced-vs-plain gate existed in code yet; the user's directive from that incident is unconditional — non-juiced runs must NEVER use potions. WHY IT IS SAFE TO LEAVE THE BLOCK IN PLACE NOW: no code path starts a non-juiced run. scripts/liveRun.ts's main() gates the auto-derive on BOTH this block and --juiced (session 42, Task 14), and scripts/orchestrator.ts no longer starts dungeon runs at all (session 54 — its dungeon arm fails closed; its resolvePotionLoadout, which gated on this block ALONE and called runOnce with no juicedStartRun, is deleted). tests/orchestrator/dungeonArmClosed.test.ts pins both halves. IF THE ORCHESTRATOR'S DUNGEON ARM IS EVER REOPENED, THE REMOVE-AFTER-USE CONVENTION COMES BACK WITH IT — or the missing --juiced gate gets built first. Absence of this block still means 0 potions loaded, full stop; that fail-safe is unchanged.
forbiddenWoods._boonPriorityComment: NOT A GATE. The user's boon-selection directive (2026-08-20, src/strategy/boonPriority.ts) is ON in live play whether or not this block exists, because it is an instruction about how to play the account, spends nothing, and is reversible by editing a list. (Until session 96 a gated sibling block sat next door -- a deliberately-suboptimal boon layer that knowingly cost run quality to buy a measurement, and therefore needed two conditions before it could fire. It was deleted; QUESTIONS.md §37 records what it was and why. The contrast is kept here because it is what explains why THIS block needs no gate.) This block exists only so the ONE number in the directive can be read without a code change. orbRule [session 58] selects how widely the per-option Hard Core payout (gigusOrbAmount) may decide: "tie-break" is the session-57 directive (payout separates options ALREADY tied at the best priority rank, and nothing else); "wide" additionally lets the payout decide when NO option matches any priority family, with rankBoons breaking payout ties. "wide" is the DEFAULT as of session 58 and was not a unilateral loosening: the session-58 brief fixed the decision rule before any number existed ("ship C if the depth loss is under 0.15 rooms"), and scripts/orbDepthExperiment.ts measured the loss at -0.002 rooms with a paired 95% CI of [-0.018, +0.014] at n=8000 per arm -- the whole interval an order of magnitude inside the bar -- buying +6.3 Hard Core per run (+10.4%). Neither setting can ever override a higher-priority boon; the wide rule only runs where the priority layer matched nothing at all. Set "tie-break" here to revert without a code change. earlyGameMaxRoom is the lifesteal demotion window: rooms 1..N are early game, and inside it a lifesteal boon is not eligible for a priority match (it falls through to rankBoons rather than being excluded). 8 is USER-CONFIRMED, not a placeholder. The sim is the exception in the other direction: its default arm stays the unmodified rankBoons path so historical numbers stay comparable — scripts/sim.ts --boon-priority runs this one.

dendren._comment: Session 13, Task 9's first live fishing budget: 100/5, conservative-first-session posture, session-13 comment retained below for history. Session 15: raised to 200/15 per the session-15 brief's direct instruction ('start live fishing casts early... the user reports 15 casts available today; raise the fishing session cap') — mineFishPatterns.ts (Task 11) needs real transition volume and the daily guard resets, so today's own allowance should actually be used rather than left idle at the old 5-cast conservative figure. 200 energy covers 16 tier-1 casts (12 energy each) with margin over the requested 15; config/discovered.json's maxCastsPerDay (10, non-juiced) is the GAME's own inferred cap and is untested past 5 casts/day — if the live loop hits a real server-side cap below 15, it fails closed (CLAUDE.md §5) rather than guessing past it. Original session-13 note: maxCastsPerSession set conservatively at 5 to match Task 9's staged gate (dry-run, one cast, then five) rather than the game's own maxCastsPerDay cap — same conservative-first-session posture as forbiddenWoods' original 3-run figure (session 08). Tier-1 casts (12 energy, the free tier — SPEC-fishing.md §3) are what the live loop uses unless told otherwise. [VERIFY] CONFIRMED [live, 2026-08-16/17]: this IS the same account-wide pool forbiddenWoods spends from. Both liveFishing.ts and liveRun.ts hit real-energy-floor guard trips (HTTP 400 on start_run) within ~10 minutes of each other, both against the SAME GET /offchain/player/energy reading (10, of 420 max, regenPerHour 18) — one pool, not two. dailyEnergyBudget above is this bot's own policy ceiling per game mode, layered on top of the one real account ceiling; hitting the real floor fails closed regardless of how much of either policy ceiling remains unspent. Session 21: raised to 240/20 — two independent sources agree on this number. `config/discovered.json`'s `dendren.maxCastsPerDayJuiced` was probe-captured back in session 11 (20 casts/day juiced, vs 10 non-juiced) but never wired into policy; the user independently confirmed this session that the real daily cast limit is 20 at 12 energy each (240 total). Not a fresh guess — the probe data and the user's own figure land on the same number.
dendren._dailyEnergyBudgetComment93: [session 93 §4] RAISED 240 -> 252 by explicit user approval 2026-08-24, to permit the day's TWENTIETH and final cast, and CONFIRMED STANDING by the user in the same session — this is the budget now, not a one-day exception, so do not revert it to 240. The repo's own 240 ceiling was reached at 19 casts while the GAME's ledger (dayDocs[pondId 2]) still showed 19/20, so the repo guard — not the game — was the binding constraint, and an unspent cast expires at the 11:00 PT rollover. CLAUDE.md's ask-first list covers spending above this budget, which is why it was approved rather than assumed. SAFE TO LEAVE AT 252: 252/12 = 21 casts, and the GAME caps the day at 20 (maxCastsPerDayJuiced), so this value can never buy a cast the server would not already refuse. It is a ceiling that has stopped being the binding one, not a loosened cap.
dendren._dailyEnergyBudgetComment107: [session 107, 2026-08-29] RAISED 252 -> 300 (21 -> 25 casts) by explicit user directive, given directly in chat, not derived. This directly resolves STATE.md sessions 105/106 open question 2: session 106's brief could not spend its one requested fishing cast because the repo's 252/252 ceiling was already exhausted from session 105 (21 casts played) while the GAME's own ledger (dayDocs[pondId 2]) still read 19/20 — the repo guard, not the game, was binding, and the gap is JEBAITOR (§34, ~9% of casts don't count against dayDocs, so more casts get PLAYED than get CHARGED). 252 was sized as 21 x 12 on the assumption the repo ceiling could 'never buy a cast the server would not already refuse' — true only when every cast charges the ledger, which JEBAITOR falsifies. 300 = 25 x 12 gives headroom for a day with several JEBAITOR procs, not a claim that 25 real casts will ever be charged. THIS DOES NOT RAISE THE GAME'S REAL CAP. `dendren.maxCastsPerDayJuiced` (discovered.json) is still 20 charged casts/day; dayDocs and/or the server's own preflight remain the true ceiling and fail closed exactly as before if hit. If a session's ledger stops the loop before 25 casts are played, that is normal — it means either the game's own 20-charge cap bound first, or JEBAITOR simply didn't proc enough today to open extra headroom above it. Do not read a sub-25 outcome as this budget being wrong.
dendren._oilsComment: [session 61 §4c] User decision 2026-08-20: oils are spent AUTONOMOUSLY within this budget, not per-cast approval. Fishing stays autonomous. THREE fields, and the third is the one with no potions analogue. allowedItemIds: 942 Mid Focus Oil (FishingRestoreFocus +2) and 937 Mid Relaxing Oil (FishingDamageFish +2 — direct fish damage despite the name); both VERIFIED against fixtures/fishing-casts/item-metadata-sample.json, SPEC-fishing §4a addendum, not taken from the brief's table. maxPerCast: the board state exposes 3 consumable slots (fishingConsumableSlotUsed), so 3 is the hard ceiling; this may be lower, never higher. policyApproved: CLAUDE.md rule 4 — FALSE until the user has seen and approved a derived consumption-timing policy (scripts/oilTimingSweep.ts). Authorising the BUDGET is not authorising the TIMING, and this is what stops liveFishing.ts's Relaxing-Oil call site (live since session 44, inert only because the balance has always been 0) from firing by itself the moment crafting finishes. ABSENCE OF THIS BLOCK STILL MEANS ZERO OILS SPENT — silence is not authorization, the session-24 lesson. Set policyApproved true only after approving a policy. [session 62 §1] APPROVED BY THE USER 2026-08-20 — policyApproved is now TRUE and oils are spent live. The approved policy is `on-demand` (handoff/OIL-POLICY.md, src/strategy/fishing/oilTiming.ts): Relaxing Oil ONLY when lethal (fishHp <= 2), Focus Oil ONLY when the focus meter is at zero. It replaces session 43's heuristic (c), which is dominated on this repo's own numbers — +4.51pp for 2630 oils against the lethal trigger's +4.47pp for 1821, i.e. indistinguishable benefit for 44% more oil. The user also confirmed the two oils cost roughly the same to craft, so the sweep's POOLED ranking stands and no per-item gate is needed. MANA: RESOLVED, user-stated 2026-08-20 — use_fishing_item does NOT consume mana, only playing cards does. That was the load-bearing assumption under OIL-POLICY.md's +19.40pp and it is now confirmed rather than assumed. STOCK: the user holds a few oils, fewer than a batch needs, and on-demand spends ~0.70/cast, so stock runs out MID-batch. A trigger firing with zero stock degrades to ordinary play (an empty consumable is an EXPECTED state, not a rule-5 unexpected one) and flags the cast OIL-POLICY-DRY, which keeps it out of BOTH outcome arms — see src/strategy/fishing/oilCastState.ts. [session 69 §4] User directive 2026-08-21: "Continue using Focus oil until supply naturally depletes, then only use 2x Relaxing oil per fishing run." perItemMaxPerCast expresses BOTH halves. Focus (942) is ABSENT from the map, which means uncapped — unconstrained until stock reaches zero, at which point the existing OIL-POLICY-DRY path records it and the batch reports rather than silently changing behaviour. Relaxing (937) is capped at 2 PER CAST; "per fishing run" is read as per cast because start_run is the server's own action for starting one cast (SPEC-fishing §2), so the directive's word is the API's word. A ceiling never causes a spend — it can only refuse an oil the policy already wanted — which is why applying it before the Focus supply runs out is safe rather than premature. A third Relaxing trigger in one cast records OIL-POLICY-DRY with reason per_cast_cap, the cast continues, the batch does not halt. [session 93 §1] USER DIRECTIVE 2026-08-24: RELAXING-OIL-ONLY. 942 (Mid Focus Oil) is REMOVED from allowedItemIds. This is a POLICY WITHDRAWAL, not a stock artifact: Focus stock has read 0 for four consecutive batches, but the point of the change is that the bot will not attempt Focus Oil even if stock is ever replenished. mayConsumeOil already rejects any id absent from this list (src/strategy/fishing/oilPolicy.ts ~line 251), so this line is the whole enforcement. perItemMaxPerCast keeps only the 937 cap; Focus's ABSENCE from that map now means 'never spent' rather than 'uncapped', because allowedItemIds decides first. ALSO LANDED, and it is the half a config-only change would have got wrong: scripts/liveFishing.ts now DROPS a withdrawn kind from oilWanted BEFORE the spend loop (event oil_trigger_policy_withdrawn). Without that, a focus trigger on an empty bag still took the held <= 0 branch and logged oil_trigger_no_stock, which flags the cast OIL-POLICY-DRY and keeps it out of BOTH outcome arms — so every future cast whose meter hit zero would have been excluded from the corpus forever, for an oil the policy no longer wants. A trigger the policy has withdrawn is not a dry bag.
